questions.question: A 'Mature Cystic Teratoma' (Dermoid) characteristically contains which feature on ultrasound?
choices: Echogenic fatty component and a 'Rokitansky nodule' (dermoid plug)
questions.detail: These contain elements from all three germ layers, often including fat and hair.

questions.question: What is the classic 'MRI hallmark' for a dermoid cyst?
choices: Loss of signal on fat-saturated sequences
Bright on T2 and bright on T1 with NO fat suppression
questions.detail: The macroscopic fat in a dermoid will 'drop out' on fat-suppressed images.

questions.question: 'Ovarian torsion' most commonly presents on ultrasound with:
choices: An enlarged, edematous ovary with peripheral follicles and a 'whirlpool' sign of the pedicle
questions.detail: Venous and lymphatic obstruction leads to massive ovarian enlargement.

questions.question: Which O-RADS category represents a 'Classic Benign' lesion (e.g., simple cyst, dermoid, or endometrioma) with <1% risk of malignancy?
questions.detail: O-RADS 2 lesions are almost certainly benign and generally do not require surgical intervention in pre-menopausal women.

questions.question: An 'Endometrioma' characteristically demonstrates which feature on T2-weighted MRI?
choices: 'T2 shading' (progressive loss of signal on T2 compared to T1)
questions.detail: The high concentration of iron and protein from old blood causes this signal drop.

questions.question: 'Polycystic Ovary Syndrome' (PCOS) is diagnosed sonographically (Rotterdam criteria) when an ovary contains at least how many follicles?
questions.detail: These are typically 2–9 mm in size and arranged peripherally (the 'string of pearls' sign).

questions.question: 'Meigs syndrome' is a triad of an ovarian fibroma, ascites, and:
questions.detail: The fluid typically resolves once the benign ovarian fibroma is removed.

questions.question: 'Struma ovarii' is a specialized teratoma composed primarily of:
questions.detail: It can even cause clinical hyperthyroidism.

questions.question: Which ovarian lesion has a characteristic 'lacey' or 'cobweb' internal echo pattern on ultrasound?
questions.detail: This represents fibrin strands during blood clot retraction.

questions.question: Ovarian 'Serous Cystadenocarcinoma' frequently presents with which finding on CT?
choices: Psammomatous calcifications and complex cystic/solid components
questions.detail: These are the most common type of malignant ovarian tumor.

questions.question: A 'Krukenberg tumor' refers to:
choices: Metastatic disease to the ovary, characteristically from a GI primary (e.g., stomach)
questions.detail: These are typically bilateral solid masses.

questions.question: 'Ovarian vein thrombosis' is a postpartum complication most commonly involving the:
questions.detail: The right vein is longer and more prone to compression during pregnancy/delivery.

questions.question: A 'paraovarian cyst' is distinguished from an ovarian cyst on ultrasound by:
choices: Demonstrating a 'separate' ovary from the cyst (sliding sign)
questions.detail: These arise from the broad ligament rather than the ovary itself.

questions.question: 'Theca lutein cysts' are large, bilateral multiloculated cysts associated with:
choices: Gestational trophoblastic disease (molar pregnancy) or fertility drugs
questions.detail: They result from extremely high levels of hCG.

questions.question: A solid ovarian mass that is 'very dark' (hypointense) on T2-weighted MRI is likely a:
questions.detail: Dense fibrous tissue has very low signal on T2WI.
